stemMd: A trapezium has parallel sides of length $14$ cm and $8$ cm and a height of $6$ cm. A triangle has a base of $12$ cm and the same area as the trapezium. What is the height of the triangle?
explanationMd:
Work out the area of the trapezium first, then run the triangle formula backwards.

The area of a trapezium is the **average** of the two parallel sides multiplied by the height:

$$A = \frac{14 + 8}{2} \times 6 = 11 \times 6 = 66 \text{ cm}^2$$

The area of a triangle is half the base times the height, so with base $12$ cm and area $66$ cm$^2$:

$$\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times h = 66$$
$$6h = 66$$
$$h = 11 \text{ cm}$$

**How to check.** Substitute back: $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times 11 = 66$, which matches the trapezium’s area. A second sanity check is a rough size estimate: the trapezium is $6$ cm tall and averages $11$ cm wide, while the triangle is only $12$ cm wide at its base and tapers to a point, so it must be noticeably taller than $6$ cm to hold the same area. That rules out any answer below about $8$ cm immediately.

Remember that a wrong answer costs $-0.2$ on this test and an omission costs nothing, so a quick substitution check is worth the ten seconds it takes.

distractorRationale.d: This comes from dropping the factor of $\frac{1}{2}$ in the triangle formula: computing $12h = 66$ gives $h = 5.5$. The area of a triangle is half the base times the height, not the base times the height.
distractorRationale.a: This comes from using only the longer parallel side for the trapezium, $14 \times 6 = 84$, and then solving $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times h = 84$ to get $h = 14$. The trapezium formula uses the average of the two parallel sides, not the longer one.
distractorRationale.b: This comes from forgetting to halve the sum of the parallel sides: $(14 + 8) \times 6 = 132$, then $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times h = 132$ gives $h = 22$. That doubles the true area of the trapezium.

accessibilityText: A trapezium has two parallel sides measuring 14 centimetres and 8 centimetres and a height of 6 centimetres. A triangle has a base of 12 centimetres and the same area as that trapezium. Find the height of the triangle.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Trapezium area = ((14+8)/2) x 6 = 11 x 6 = 66 cm^2; setting (1/2) x 12 x h = 66 gives 6h = 66, h = 11 cm. 22 cm results from dropping the factor 1/2 and 5.5 cm from halving twice, so neither is defensible.
